sense.text:
“So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations.” The question is what occurred prophetically within those fourteen generations: what happened from David to Babylon, and what happened from Babylon to Christ. This verse is very important because Christians tend to ignore it.

From David to Babylon: when Solomon died his son Rehoboam took over, and under Rehoboam the kingdom was split into two, the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. After they split, the northern kingdom went into the Assyrian captivity. After the Assyrian captivity came the Babylonian captivity under Nebuchadnezzar: he conquered the southern kingdom, and he took all Assyria, which included the northern kingdom, into captivity.

“From the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ”: after the Babylonian captivity came the Persian and Mede captivity; after that came the Greek captivity that Christians don’t know nothing about; after the Greek captivity came the Roman captivity. Now under Rome, Christ is born.

precepts.why:
“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus: for he shall save his people from their sins.” That was the purpose of the Messiah. Through all those generations we kept going from captivity to captivity to captivity to captivity, and now the Saviour is born.

That’s what Christians missed. They say, no, no, let’s start at verse 18, about the birth with Mary; they back up and skip the fourteen generations of captivity that the Messiah was born to save his people from.

Now Christ prophesies something under the Roman captivity. “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: Christ told the Israelites you’re going to fall by the edge of the sword, because at that time you had Judah, Benjamin, Levi and a small remnant of the northern kingdom in the land. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: Rome would destroy us by the edge of the sword and we would be led away as slaves into all nations.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: who would live in Jerusalem? Gentiles, meaning non-Israelites. Christians read it and say, oh no, they’re back in the land. No: Christ said they would not be back in the land “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”, until the time of the Gentile rulership is finished. Are the Gentiles still ruling today? So who’s in the land? Gentiles. I don’t see why a Christian can’t figure that out.

sense.text:
“Thy prophets have seen vain and foolish things for thee”: the prophets of our people have seen vain and foolish things for us, and vain and foolish things mean lies. They’ve seen lies for our people.

“And they have not discovered thine iniquity, to turn away thy captivity”: discovering our iniquity means telling us why we as a people went into slavery, why we as a people are continually oppressed century after century. These prophets, these pastors, have not done it. By telling us why we went into slavery, which was breaking God’s commandments, they would turn away our captivity. Christ came, he taught us to keep the commandments, he died on the cross for us; we would know that in order to get out of this captivity we’ve got to keep the commandments in the faith of Christ. But our pastors have not done that.

“But have seen for thee false burdens”: Christmas is a false burden. You spend all your money a month before Christmas, check after check, making sure your kids get some damn Christmas gifts, making sure you got a big stupid Christmas tree with some bulbs on it, and that ain’t got nothing to do with Christ. Easter is another false burden: you spend all your money on some Easter clothes, Mama gotta have the big stupid hat, the boy’s gotta have a stupid three-piece suit, then you spend money on some damn eggs. Rabbits never laid eggs.

Anniversaries are another false burden. Some of you women get divorced because your husband forgot that stupid day: you forgot our anniversary, I want a divorce, you don’t love me. And you brothers spend thousands of dollars on that daggone ring, and that ring comes from ancient Egypt. If you don’t buy her a fifteen thousand dollar ring you don’t love her? You could use that money for a down payment on a house, but she has convinced you to get two and three jobs to buy her a damn ring that costs more than a mortgage. And some brothers, after they get married, want her paying their rent; you just spent fifteen grand, and now you want help paying your rent? That makes no sense. These are false burdens that we burden ourselves with.

“And causes of banishment”: we’re banished from the kingdom of heaven because we’re following false burdens: wedding anniversaries, Christmas, Kwanzaa, the Hajj, birthdays, Valentine’s Day, Mama’s Day. You’re spending all your money on that foolishness. All them things are false burdens, and they cause us to be banished from God’s kingdom because those are all lies that we’re following. You’re not going to enter the kingdom because of Christmas or Easter or an anniversary.

“All that pass by clap their hands at thee”: all the nations clapped their hands at us. “They hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem”: we are the daughter of Jerusalem. “Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty”: are these the twelve tribes of Israel that once ruled the world from the time of Moses, Joshua, David and Solomon? Are these those people? “The joy of the whole earth”: these were the joy of the whole earth.

“All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee”: all our enemies, these other nations, have opened their mouth against us. “They hiss and gnash the teeth: they say, We have swallowed her up”: the nations said we have swallowed up the twelve tribes of Israel. “Certainly this is the day that we looked for”: why? Because now we’re all oppressed in captivity. “We have found, we have seen it.” We’ve fallen from a long way.

Write this down: the curses can be summarized in four things, slavery, colonialism, loss of identity and oppression. Those four things summarize Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68, what would happen to the twelve tribes of Israel.

“Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee”: those curses would follow us, pursue us and overtake us, “till thou be destroyed.” We’ve been destroyed as a people, as a nation. “Because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded thee”: all those curses God mentions in this chapter, slavery, colonialism, loss of identity and oppression, happened to us because we broke God’s commandments.

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign”: these curses would be upon the Israelites for a sign to identify us as the Israelites. When you see a people in the earth who suffer slavery, oppression, colonialism and loss of identity, those are the Israelites, those are the twelve tribes of Israel. “And for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever”: how long would those things be upon us? Forever. That’s the prophecy right there.

precepts.why:
What we just read in Deuteronomy 28 says the curses will be upon us forever, meaning a long time, and even the Apocrypha says the same thing. “I will liken my judgment unto a ring”: a ring goes round and round and around, so God’s judgments are like a ring, they go round and round: Assyria, Babylon, Persia and Media, Greece, Rome.

Christians say, oh, it stopped with Rome. It didn’t stop with Rome, because Christ said in Luke 21:24 we would fall by the edge of the sword and be led away captive into all nations. So it didn’t just end with Rome; Christians don’t know what the hell they’re talking about. “Like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” Christians say captivity for the Israelites ended with Rome; we already proved that’s a lie. Christ said it’s a lie.

sense.text:
This is when they set up the Kaaba: Muhammad put that black stone in it. An old painting from antiquities, a long, long time ago, shows their black rock inside that cube, and people from all around the world kiss the stone; Kaaba means Black Stone. A photo now of them with the black stone in Mecca shows them dressed exactly the same as the painting. Everyone’s doing it, Hajj: you’ve got to go there once in your lifetime and kiss the black stone. Brothers, sisters, that’s called idolatry.

“Saying to a stock, Thou art my father”: a stock is wood, saying to a piece of wood, thou art my father. “And to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth.” That’s all idolatry. When you pray to wood and stone, that’s idolatry, that’s breaking God’s commandments.

Now the Arab slave trade. A lot of us don’t like to talk about it, and black Muslims definitely never want to talk about it, but it’s our reality. This is read to show it is not based upon any kind of racial rhetoric; it’s strictly biblical.

“Lift up thine eyes unto the high places, and see where thou hast not been lien with”: lien with means corrupted, see where you have not been corrupted. “In the ways hast thou sat for them, as the Arabian in the wilderness”: we sat for the Arabians in the wilderness. It’s talking about slavery, and that’s when they forced Islam on some of us.

The drawings show them bringing us into captivity from the east coast of Africa, our mothers and fathers on the ground, our sons walking behind; this is what they don’t talk about in schools or churches. They show our mothers, daughters, aunts and grandmothers in the slave markets; one of our mothers as a young girl sitting on the ground, a slave to the Arab women; brothers as slaves, young boys, some of them castrated. They forced Islam on our people through rape, robbery and torture. They made some of us their personal bodyguards and butlers, and any male who was a bodyguard or butler to a girl was castrated; he became a eunuch, they cut his penis off. You black brothers and sisters in Islam don’t want to talk about it; well, we’re going to talk about it, because the Bible talks about this.

The book Slavery in the Arab World by Murray Gordon tells of the slave markets of Mecca and Jeddah, where pilgrims coming from Iraq, Syria, Persia and other parts of the Middle East bought slaves and brought them back. When they went on their Hajj they brought us back as slaves. Mecca was a slave market; stop fooling yourselves, it’s never been holy. The blood of our ancestors covers that land. They sold us there, they killed us there, they raped us there; I don’t care how they dazzle it up to make it look pretty, what’s holy about it? Malcolm missed the slave trade in Mecca by two years; he would have been a slave.

The transatlantic slave trade lasted four centuries, but the trans-Saharan slave trade continued for seventeen centuries, from 652 to 1960, and some books say it started with the so-called Prophet Muhammad, around 610 AD. And it didn’t end in 1960: an article of April 17, 2023 shows they’ve been selling us in Libya since Gaddafi died, with European Union money. A United Nations investigation found forced labor, sexual slavery and torture: forced labor is what they did to the men, sexual slavery is what they did to the women, and torture to both of us if we did not submit to the will of Allah. The EU is complicit, and it all popped off once they killed Gaddafi in the once prosperous nation of Libya.

Then an earthquake or flood happens over there and y’all are crying. They were just selling your brothers and sisters and raping your sisters, and you’re crying for Libya? Are you insane? God sends judgment on them, and we say look what’s going on, let’s pray for them. God says, what is wrong with my people? I’m bringing judgment for what these people did to their people, and they’re over there crying. This is why we’re an unseen government. We’re the only race on earth that would do such stupidity: you cry out for vengeance, and when God brings the vengeance on your enemies you cry and pray for them. That makes no sense.

Coming off the history of the transatlantic slave trade, the pictures of us with yokes of iron on our necks, Deuteronomy 28:48, and the slave ships of Deuteronomy 28:68.

“Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave?” Are the Israelites servants? Why does he say is Israel a servant, is he a homeborn slave? Because every time you read the Bible the Israelites are always in captivity: from captivity to captivity to captivity to captivity.

“Why is he spoiled?” Why is he oppressed and robbed? That is us.

Something about our people: we’re the only race that does not desire to rule the planet Earth. Anytime we’re on the street discussing world dominion, the first thing our brothers and sisters say is ‘can a white man be with us?’ White men don’t ask that about us. Here God shows how the nations feel about rulership.

“Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming”: the hell is talking about the nations. “It stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth”: that’s the proof right there, the dead, the hell, are the chief ones of the earth. “It hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.”
“All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?” “Thy pomp is brought down to the grave”: thy pomp, thy pride, is brought down to the grave.

precepts.why:
That’s really what was wanted: “All the kings of the nations, even all of them, lie in glory, every one in his own house.” All the nations are waiting for their opportunity to rule, to have world dominion when America is destroyed. They all lie in wait for their glory.

We are the only race that does not desire it or lie in wait for glory; we’re the only people that want to be subservient. Men under the will of their woman: you’re not fit to rule being a mama’s boy. Chasing behind a woman, you’re not a leader; you’re simple. Just sit on the sidelines and suck your thumb.

sense.text:
This is the state of our men, and why many of us don’t desire to rule.

“Thy sons have fainted”: fainted means we have lost consciousness. We have fainted from God’s truth, we have fainted from our identity, we have fainted from keeping God’s laws.

“They lie at the head of all the streets”: our young men hang at the head of all the streets, hanging on the corners. If you ever saw the series The Wire, you see us hanging on the corner; the new series on Netflix, Top Boy, you see them in England hanging on the corners. Nothing to do but sell drugs. All the music videos: sell drugs and chase women around.

“As a wild bull in a net”: our sons, uncontrollable, no discipline.

“They are full of the fury of the Lord”: full of God’s judgment, Deuteronomy 28. That’s our sons right there: let something pop off and everybody pulls out their phone for Worldstar; we love drama. “The rebuke of thy God”: Deuteronomy 28 is the rebuke of our God.
“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted”: our people are the afflicted. “And drunken, but not with wine”: we are a drunk people, but not drunk with wine. We’re drunk with lies and philosophies.

“Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling”: the cup of trembling is Deuteronomy the 28th chapter, from verse 15 on. He’s saying, I’m going to take that cup from you.

“Even the dregs of the cup of my fury”: he’s taking from us slavery, colonialism, loss of identity and oppression. How does he do that? He’s starting to restore to us our identity, who we are: Israelites. We got to keep the Commandments. That’s him taking the cup from us.

“Thou shalt no more drink it again”: you shall no more drink them curses of Deuteronomy 28, no more again.

“But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee”: all them curses I afflicted you with, I’m going to put them curses on that white man, them Arabs, them Hamites, all them nations that afflicted us. They go and drink Deuteronomy 28:15-68.

“Which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over”: what have the nations said to us? Bow down. It’s a spiritual thing. Bow down, so they could walk over us.

“And thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over”: we allow the nations to walk all over us. At the funeral of this freaking Queen Elizabeth they put all the African presidents on a bus, in the back of the freaking bus, and gave all the white presidents a motorcade. Total disrespect. They were smiling until they got to the actual funeral and saw all the white leaders getting out of their limos and personal vehicles while they were getting off the bus. Nobody gave them a memo; they didn’t have enough regard for them to tell them what was going on. Take what the hell we give you.

Anytime a white woman gets kidnapped or killed they find a guy right away; a black woman or our sons get kidnapped and killed, they can’t figure out who did it. Case closed, cold case.

They walk all over us. They say Jesus is white; you come with a scripture and they say we don’t give a damn about that, he’s white, and that’s what we’re going to teach you. You say Christopher Columbus never discovered America, there were people already here; they say we don’t give a damn what you say, you’re going to teach it to your kids too, and if you don’t bring your kids to school we’re going to put you in jail.

Out of the book Before the Mayflower: Denmark Vesey was free and burned with hatred of slavery and slaveholders. He read to the slaves from the Bible how the children of Israel were delivered out of Egypt, he quoted Joshua everywhere he went, and he warned that God helps those who help themselves: get off your black ashy behinds and stop being a slave. When slaves bowing to white men in the street answered him ‘but we are slaves’, he said ‘you deserve to be slaves.’ You bow to white folks: what the hell is wrong with you? They’re not God. Slaves with that attitude deserve to be slaves. It’s the same with these Christians that come against us teaching the Bible but never go against the white man with white Jesus; we double dog dare you to do videos on it.

Then Vesey switched from the role of agitator to the role of organizer. This is what gets you agitated.

“The fruit of thy land, and all thy labours”: that’s your natural resources. “Shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up”: we’re seeing that today in society, and it has been going on for a long time.

“And thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway”: one of the curses is that we’ll be oppressed and crushed always.
“So that thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see”: that’s an agitator. God says this constant oppression is going to make you mad for the things that you see.

precepts.why:
Like Denmark Vesey, you go from agitator to organizer. “Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad”: oppression makes a wise man mad, and that’s when you’re becoming an organizer. You go from being just pissed off at the things you see, the conditions you see, to using wisdom and saying, you know what, I need to organize the people; we need to do something about this constant oppression.

Big burly black men bowing down to white men and white women, and don’t say you don’t bow down to the white woman.

sense.text:
Back to the last verse of Isaiah 51, where we laid our body as the ground and as the street for the nations to go over, and keep reading into chapter 52.

“Awake, awake”: that’s the warning to us. He’s telling us to wake up. You got your body on the ground, your soul on the ground, letting all the nations walk all over you; now God’s message to us is awake.

“Put on thy strength, O Zion”: keep these Commandments as Israelites. “Put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem”: putting on your beautiful garments means keeping the Commandments, and literally putting back on the dress code of Israel.

“For henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean”: he’s saying, I’m going to take these unclean nations off your back.

“Shake thyself from the dust”: because in the last chapter we were laying down on the ground letting people walk all over us. Wake up.

“Arise, and sit down”: sit down means study. Learn your history, learn the testimonies of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, get your mind right, get focused, organize yourselves. “O Jerusalem: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion.”

precepts.why:
From the prophecies in the Old Testament to the prophecies in the New Testament, saying the same thing. “Knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep”: awake out of sleep again. Get off the ground, wake up and get out of the bed. “For now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.”

“The night is far spent”: the night is your captivity, and it’s far spent. “The day is at hand”: the truth is here. Now you know you’re Israelites; wake up.

“Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness”: cast off your sins, your adultery, your fornication, your lying, your stealing, your abominations. “And let us put on the armour of light”: that’s God’s laws, God’s Commandments.

sense.text:
“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: it’s talking about Christ.

“And the government shall be upon his shoulder”: right now Christ is establishing government, one universal, omnipotent government. He’s not establishing a church group, he’s not establishing a choir, he’s establishing a government. Men especially, get your mind right and understand government. Some of us understand the club, the party over here, but when it comes to government: what’s that about? This is why we’ve got to get our minds right and focus.

“The mighty God”: that goes back to all the things you read from the time of Genesis.

“The everlasting Father”: you might be confused about the Everlasting Father, but like John 1, Christ is the one that created all things. Christ is not the Father, but he’s our father: he made us, he is our creator.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end”: it’s never going to end. “Upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever”: this is why we’re going to learn the laws of God; he’s going to establish it with judgment. “The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”
“The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel”: he gave us this word, and we’re supposed to understand it. Brothers and sisters, the Lord is setting up a government.

precepts.why: On the Everlasting Father. “These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God”: Christ is the beginning of the creation of God.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God”: notice, with God. “And the Word was God.” So you’ve got two right there: God the Father and God the Son. “The same was in the beginning with God.”

“All things were made by him”: who’s the him? The Word, Christ. “And without him was not any thing made that was made”: without Christ was not anything made.

Watch what Christ said: “And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.” Christ says you’ve never heard the Father’s voice or seen his shape at any time. Do you understand what at any time means?

We thought we were dealing with the Father in the wilderness. That wasn’t the Father. Remember when we said we don’t want to hear you, Moses, we want to hear the Lord, and the voice thundered and the earth shook and quaked: you thought that was the Father. Christ said you never heard his voice at any time.

Even at the Transfiguration, when you heard the voice say ‘this is my beloved Son, hear ye him’: that wasn’t the Father, because Christ already said you never heard his voice at any time. That was an ambassador speaking on his behalf.

The question is, when are we going to see the Father? Remember Philip said, Lord, show us the Father and it sufficeth us, and Christ said, have I been so long time with you, Philip, have you not known me? The one you think is the Father: Christ is telling him, I made you, I’m your creator. Christ is not the Father, but he’s our father.

“And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads.” And the verse above it: “And there shall be no more curse”: this is the kingdom. “But the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him.”

“And they shall see his face”: that’s when we’re going to see the Father’s face. His name in their foreheads: that’s when we’re going to know the Father’s true name. Not now, brothers, but on that day.

sense.text:
This is the rise of an unseen government. I want you men to understand that the rise, the rebuilding of true Israel, is the rise of an unseen government, because they don’t see us as nothing. Even our sisters look at us and say, you ain’t nothing. I’m just telling you the truth.

“Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother”: the white man sits and speaks against us; Esau sits and speaks against Jacob. That’s what it’s talking about. “Thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”: Esau slanders his own mother’s son, which is Jacob.

“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence”: the Lord kept silent. “Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”: they thought God surely got to be a white man, because they ain’t been judged yet. That’s the white man’s mentality: he ain’t did nothing to us; we jacked his people up and we’re still getting away with it scot-free; surely God’s a white man.

“But I will reprove thee”: God says don’t worry, I will correct you, I will reprove you. “And set them in order before thine eyes”: that’s you men and women, set in order.

We are moving under the radar. People don’t see; even people that watch us on video don’t take us serious. They look at us always arguing, fighting, always in the midst of adultery and selling drugs. Hey brothers, nobody’s gonna see us coming.

precepts.why:
Paul says it: in my absence I’m beholding your order. “For though I be absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, joying and beholding your order, and the stedfastness of your faith in Christ.” There was always order set up.

When they say that among black people there’s no such thing as order, that’s a lie. We’re the only race that says that. When you hear white people telling you that, ask the white man: if there’s no order, no ranking structure, then why has your government got to rank in order and structure? Why do the Chinese got rank and structure? Why do the Arabs got to rank and structure government? How come blacks and Latinos are the only ones that don’t understand rank, structure and order? It’s a trick; they’re deceiving us. God is setting us in order.

sense.text:
“Again, there is another that is slow”: that’s us, brothers and sisters, we’re slow. We don’t catch things right away. You’ll be at camp, and there’ll be an Edomite and an Israelite listening, and you say Jesus Christ is black. The black man will say it don’t matter. The white man will say, I’m going into slavery: he’s already added one plus one equals two. The black man and the black woman is slow as hell: it doesn’t matter what he looks like. The white guy figured it out already.

“And hath need of help”: we’re the ones that always need help. “Wanting ability”: we lack ability. “And full of poverty”: our people is full of poverty. Now watch: “yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate”.

“And lifted up his head from misery”: he said, my people is miserable, let me lift up their head. “So that many that saw it marvelled at him”: everybody that sees us rise is gonna marvel. This is that low-life, no-good people, and God’s raising them up. Everybody that sees this shall marvel. It’s the prophecy.

“Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of the Lord.” “Wisdom, knowledge, and understanding of the law, are of the Lord”: understanding of what? Of the law. “Love, and the way of good works, are from him.”

They ain’t gonna see us coming, brothers and sisters. They’re gonna continue to mock us and continue to disrespect us. The Lord says don’t worry: when y’all together and you organize yourselves, the Holy Spirit is there amongst you.

“He raiseth up the poor out of the dust”: it’s a prophecy. “And lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill.” You mad because Trump said what he said about Africa? He didn’t lie. What you mad for? We went from dominating and ruling the entire planet earth to this, and when somebody says it you get mad? God just said it; go get mad at God now. The dunghill is poverty, this situation. I don’t care how much money you got, you’re still in a dunghill; you got a crumb in this society compared to what God had given us.

“To set them among princes”: you would look at this brother on the screen and go, hell no, he could not be a prince, never ever; look where he lives; nothing good can come out of that. But don’t worry, there is a God. He’s gonna set us among princes. “And to make them inherit the throne of glory”: he’s gonna make us inherit the kingdom forever.

“For the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them”: that means not only are we gonna run this earth, we gonna run the universe.

Listen good, brothers and sisters: “the Spirit of the Lord will come upon” you men and women when you get the Holy Spirit, and the Holy Spirit is not emotional. That’s for you women that feel tingly, like I did in church. God ain’t dealing with your emotions; he’s dealing with logic, he’s dealing with knowledge.

This is what God said to Saul in the book of Samuel: the spirit will come upon you and you’ll be changed into another man. That is the change that has to come over every one of us in this truth.

precepts.why:
By him, God is a God of knowledge. “Talk no more so exceeding proudly”: proudly in sin, that’s what it’s talking about. “Let not arrogancy come out of your mouth”: arrogancy in the context of sin, don’t let it come out of your mouth. How much money you stole today? I stole eight thousand dollars from Deacon Malachi. You truck drivers out here know what I’m talking about. Don’t speak proudly, brothers, in your sin.

“For the Lord is a God of knowledge”: does it say emotion? Knowledge. So you sisters, God ain’t dealing with your emotions; he don’t give a damn about emotions, it means nothing.

“And by him actions are weighed”: based on the knowledge you men and you women got, your actions will be weighed, will be judged. He ain’t judging you on your emotions, oh I’m angry; he don’t give a damn. What are you doing with the knowledge he gave you? That goes with the talents he gave, to some ten, to some five: what did you do with the knowledge God gave you? Sisters, did you teach your children right? Did you teach them laws while your husband was out at work? No, I didn’t feel like it, the soap operas were on, I couldn’t get time for it. Now your son’s a sodomite, and she’s blaming the husband. That’s cause you wasn’t home; you were sitting at home watching BET and Atlanta housewives.

God’s judging your actions based on the knowledge you got, and that includes the sisters that get mad and want a divorce over some stupid stuff, and then after the divorce want to come back to IUIC. This is not that type of a party. You’re not gonna divorce your husband and then come back and get another man: that’s whoredom, sister. The knowledge you learn should have taught you the difference. You married him; he was good enough to sex you, but he’s not good enough to lead you and guide you? Then you complain he don’t got a job, when you knew he didn’t have a job when you got with him. One father told a brother who wanted his daughter, show me you can maintain the same job for two years and I’ll give you my daughter, and that’s good thinking. That’s for the bum brothers that work six months, always get fired and collect unemployment. Get a job; that’s part of getting yourself together. God is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.

sense.text: “That ye present your bodies a living sacrifice”: be willing to sacrifice your life for this truth when the time comes for it. “Holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” Why is it your reasonable service? Because the Son of God died for you. You mean to tell me he’s not worth you giving your life for? And they can only kill the body, brothers; they cannot kill the inner man, the soul.

“And be not conformed to this world”: there should be no sukianas in here, no sexy Reds in here. A sister sees a brother she likes; he’s so handsome, but he’s married. So she gets close with the brother’s wife, befriends her, takes pictures with her, asks her for counsel, all slick moves. Then: do you mind if your husband takes me to the laundromat, my car broke down? One day turns into two days, turns into a week. It happens all the time. After she sexes that brother, she says that wasn’t enough, goes to another handsome brother’s house and gives him a BJ: from brother one to brother two in the same week. Dallas, Texas: I lie not. There will be no sexy Reds up in here, no sukianas; we will throw you out. They’re passing around genital warts, and you thinking, oh she’s so pretty. Another cute, adorable sister, and it’d be an honor for a brother to marry her: no, Bishop, she just got locked up for robbing a bank. This is the people we get; everybody that comes in here, we sick, we get all kinds, and we’re just trying to work with y’all. That’s why I told them stories: be not conformed to this world.

“But be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”: we gotta change. That’s what God said to Saul in the book of Samuel: the spirit will come upon you and you’ll be changed into another man. If you are the same grimy, no-good brother from last year to this year, what you doing, bruh? Sis, you still a sukiana? You in the trucking business robbing brothers: why come in Israel and you extorting and robbing?

Around 2017 or 2018 we talked about going into real estate together, and everybody had to put in an amount. One brother, nicknamed Blackie, put in about 40 G’s. Then his sister comes in cursing him out: he stole that money from his grandma’s bank account. If he’ll steal from his grandmama, what will he do with us? From that, I’m not getting in no businesses with Israel. You truck drivers, don’t get into no businesses with fellow truckers: they will rob you, they will steal from you, they will lie to cover it up. I’m shocked at the stuff I’ve been hearing here in Atlanta: you a bunch of thieves up in here, you’re lucky you ain’t go to jail.

Be changed, brothers and sisters, by the renewing of your mind. “That ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God”: the only way you can prove what is that good and acceptable will of God is by your life, us seeing the change in you, brothers and sisters seeing the change in each other. I know where that brother came from, I know where that sister came from; she did a whole 180, she has changed her life, he has changed his life.

“Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think”: don’t get puffed up. “But to think soberly”: this is my brother, this is my sister; that’s how we gotta think soberly. “According as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.”

precepts.why:
“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives”: right now we’ve been bethinking ourselves. We are remembering who we are; the loss of identity is being taken from us; we’re remembering that we are the children of Israel, carried captive here in America. “And repent”: that’s what every man, woman, boy and girl in here is doing.

“And make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned”: this is what the Lord wants to hear in your evening, morning and noon prayers: we have sinned. “And have done perversely”: some of the stories I told you were perverse stories, but they were true. “We have committed wickedness.”

“And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies”: in this land, “which led them away captive”. That’s why they’re not going to see us coming, brothers: we’re the slaves that they destroyed, and the Lord said don’t worry, repent, I’ve got this. “And pray unto thee toward their land”: that’s why we face Jerusalem.

“Then hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy dwelling place, and maintain their cause”: it’s time, the Lord’s hearing our prayers. We want the Lord to set us back up; we want the Lord to establish Jerusalem once again. “And forgive thy people that have sinned against thee”, “For they be thy people, and thine inheritance, which thou broughtest forth out of Egypt, from the midst of the furnace of iron”.

So that’s an example of becoming another man, becoming another woman: changing, transforming. Not a Transformer; we ain’t talking about change like that. We’re talking about the inner man, the inner woman.

sense.text: “Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.” What does it mean to be born again? It is the same change: becoming another man, another woman, the inner man transformed.

precepts.why:
Here it goes. “Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding”: that’s being born again, starting all over again. Remember that song, starting all over again, it’s gonna be rough and tough. “And reform your hearts”: the word reform is change; transform your mind, change the way you think.

“Ye shall be kept alive, and after death ye shall obtain mercy”: after your body is gone, you’re gonna obtain mercy, because after this body is gone we have celestial bodies. The white man ain’t never taught you about that, but it’s true nonetheless.

Y’all think that when this body is gone, that’s it. That’s Christianity. Stop listening to Christians and stop listening to scientists; they stupid.

“There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.” Terrestrial means earth: we’re made of the earth; Adam was made of the earth, that’s terrestrial. Terra means earth. Paul is making a distinction between the terrestrial and the celestial, and celestial goes into the spirit realm.

“For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved”: the earthly house of this tabernacle is this terrestrial body. “We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens”: that’s going into the celestial.

“For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven”: Paul is saying, I want my celestial body; I’m tired of this body, because this body keeps me in sin. “If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked”: get your celestial body, but don’t be found in sin.

“For we that are in this tabernacle do groan”: this earthly, terrestrial body, we groan, “being burdened”, burdened with sin. “Not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon”: we want to be clothed upon with a celestial body, “that mortality might be swallowed up”.

Go back to First Corinthians 15 for where mortality is swallowed up. “For this corruptible must put on incorruption”: this corruptible is this body, this terrestrial body. “And this mortal must put on immortality”: your terrestrial body must put on immortality. That’s the same thing said in Second Corinthians 5.

“So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.” So there is no death, brothers and sisters. The only thing they can destroy is this flesh. The Bible’s telling you you have another body in heaven.

In The Matrix, when he came out, Morpheus said it was because you never used them; they showed you the difference between one realm and the other. They got all that from the holy scriptures. The churches just never teach us nothing; they don’t know nothing.

sense.text:
We’ll delve into this more in another class; this is just to touch on it. “Except ye be converted”: that’s what I wanted right there. “And become as little children”: meaning start all over again, like a baby. I don’t care if you’re 70 years old or 80. Moses was 80 years old when God called him, so age is no excuse; you just rebellious. Abraham was around 100 years old. If they can be that old and change, you mean your old stank self can’t change at 65 or 75? What the hell is wrong with you? You got a few years left; you better change. Become like this little child: forget all that garbage you learned.

“Ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven”: you can’t enter the kingdom of heaven unless you start all over again as a child in this truth. If you’ve been in this truth one year, you are a one-year-old child; eight years, an eight-year-old child; twelve years, a twelve-year-old child. Some brothers and sisters say, I’m grown, you don’t tell me what to do. You ain’t got that little child spirit; you got that old spirit on you. The Lord can’t use you until you decide, I want to be converted as a little child.

precepts.why: “Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?” Christ answered, “Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God: but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.” If you will enter into life, do what? Keep the commandments. Y’all understand that, brothers and sisters: he said keep the commandments.
“If ye love me, keep my commandments.” Christ said if you love me, keep my commandments. That’s what he said.

sense.text: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh”: walking in the spirit means walking in God’s laws. That’s what walk in the spirit means.

“For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary”, meaning opposite, “the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would.” There is a war, brothers and sisters, within us. Your inner man, your inner woman, the inner Christ within you wants to keep the commandments, but your flesh says no: hold on, wait a minute, get your groove on. Look at sister so-and-so, she got it going on, help her out, do this for her. But she’s married. Back in the world you did it, you can still do it; look at her smiling at you.

A true story: a brother rode with me to the Men’s Conference, kept checking his phone, hiding it, went to the bathroom. Then another brother at home looks at his wife’s phone, and she has pictures of the hotel room and the bathroom: he was taking pictures of his tallywacker and sending them to the brother’s wife. You can’t make this stuff up. And there’s many other stories. Some brothers come in this truth and they don’t change; they don’t change.

“But if ye be led of the Spirit, ye are not under the law”: meaning the law of sacrifice, the old covenant law of sacrifice. Write that down. It’s not talking about the law that says thou shall not steal; you’re still under that.

“Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery”: that’s the first. The law says thou shalt not commit adultery, and that lets you know we’re still under that law. “Fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness, Idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies, Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like”.

“Of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.” That bottom part proves that we’re still under God’s laws. If you’re doing adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness, idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies, envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and any other thing I forgot to mention, you’re not getting the kingdom, which means the law is in full effect.

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love”: love is the first one, and love is keeping God’s laws, his commandments. “Joy, peace, longsuffering”: I was watching Captain Horeb’s class this morning, and he was talking about people that are spiritual vampires. They always depressed, they always complain, they complain, they complain; they’ll suck the life out of you. Stay away from people like that. “Gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.”

Meaning there’s no law you can pull on a brother or sister that’s fulfilling the fruit of the spirit. They’re keeping the commandments: that’s the love they got. They got joy, they got peace in their life, they are long-suffering, they are gentle, they have goodness, they have faith in Christ, meekness and temperance. There’s no law you can pull to condemn them or show them that they’re wrong.

“And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.” If you’re walking in the spirit, keeping the commandments, you have crucified the flesh, because the flesh is filled with adultery, lies, fornication, stealing, uncleanness, witchcraft, hatred.
“If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.” If you live in the spirit, also walk in the spirit.

“Let us not be desirous of vain glory”: brothers and sisters, don’t be desirous of vain glory. “Provoking one another, envying one another”: don’t provoke one another to evil, don’t envy one another, don’t be jealous of each other.

precepts.why:
Here’s the precept: “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul”. What’s another word for the corruptible body, brothers? Flesh; the one we read in Corinthians, terrestrial. Your soul is the real you, and this body is made to press your soul down.

“And the earthy tabernacle”: that’s the terrestrial body, your flesh. It “weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things”. You muse on God’s laws, but this body weighs it down: I know you want to keep the commandments, but I’m here to prevent that. That is the flesh lusting against the spirit.

Christians omit the meaning of love according to the Bible. “And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.” So the fruit of the spirit is love, and that’s keeping God’s laws, his commandments.

sense.text:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”: read the Bible, brothers and sisters. The Bible is a manual. “No one of these shall fail”: no one of these prophecies shall fail.

“None shall want her mate”: you can’t mate the Bible with the Quran, you can’t mate the Bible with the Gilgamesh epics, you can’t mate the Bible with the Egyptian Book of the Dead, you can’t mate the Bible with any scientific book. “For my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.”

“And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line.” The Lord divided the prophets by line in his Bible: Obadiah got a small portion, Ezekiel got a large portion, Jeremiah got an even bigger portion, Isaiah got a large portion.

precepts.why:
When it says “no one of these shall fail”, this is what it means: “Blessed be the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.”

There hath not failed one word of all his good promise. Not one of the prophecies written in the book of the Lord shall fail.

sense.text: “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith”: I tell you how to study, I tell you to pray, I tell you to apply, but you have to build yourself up. I can’t build you up, just like you can’t build me up. It is up to every Israelite man and every Israelite woman to study, to pray, and most of all to apply, because God is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. That is why you got to build yourself up, “praying in the Holy Ghost”.

“Keep yourselves in the love of God.” Only you can keep yourself in the love of God, every man and woman. I can’t keep you in it; only you can do that. It is your fight, not mine; mine is different than yours. “Looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.”

“Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence”: write this down, diligence means persistent work. Give diligence “to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall”.

You know why some of y’all get caught up in sins? Because you have idle time, nothing to do. And brothers and sisters, there is always something to do. This truth is too big. There are too many Israelites scattered worldwide; the Bible says we number as the sands of the sea, and we have not reached most of them, and you have idle time. That’s why you are in the midst of adultery. Look at all this work we got to do.

A lot of times they think Esau’s work is what they are supposed to be occupied in, but it is the Lord’s work you are supposed to be occupied in. Don’t think you are going to show diligence in Esau’s kingdom; you are supposed to show diligence in the Lord’s business.

Remember what the Lord is setting up: a government. “Now then we are ambassadors for Christ.” An ambassador is an accredited diplomat sent by a country as its official representative to a foreign country. Brothers, you are an official representative of the kingdom of heaven, Jerusalem. The country is Jerusalem, the real Jerusalem, the heavenly Jerusalem that is coming on earth, and you are its official representative to a foreign country.

“As though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God.” Be reconciled to God means repent, return to God.

We have to start speaking like ambassadors and conducting ourselves like ambassadors. Our pants should not be below our butt. We should not look unkempt, meaning homeless; in fact there should be nobody in here homeless. We should all become well studied.

precepts.why:
That’s why the Lord said: “See, I have this day set thee over the nations”. He told Jeremiah what he said to all the prophets, all of us: I have set you over the nations. What does that mean? You are an ambassador.

“And over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.” That is our job as ambassadors for Christ. We are official diplomats.

We are ambassadors for Christ; well, if you are an ambassador, where is your country? “For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.” As ambassadors, brothers, we must declare plainly that we seek a country. “And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from whence they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.”

So we got to let everybody know we seek a country. When we go to other countries we let them know we seek a country. They say, what happened to your country? You destroyed our country, you destroyed the people, our race, you destroyed us. That is where the prophecy is going to come in; it is going to activate the angels. We are going to prophesy what they did to us as the nation of Israel and what is going to happen to them.

sense.text:
“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant”: it is a light thing for you to be my servant. As servants we are ambassadors, “to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”. That is our job, brothers and sisters.

“I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles”: the Gentiles here are Israelites in a Gentile state of mind. “That thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth”: that means we must go unto the ends of the earth together to teach and preach.

“For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal”: it has nothing to do with guns, sticks or knives; that is carnal. They are “mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. As we go as ambassadors for Christ, as servants, we are pulling down strongholds. Christianity is a stronghold. Islam is a stronghold. Atheists is a stronghold on some of our people’s minds.

“Casting down imaginations”: we got to cast down all imaginations. You might imagine Christ is white, but we gonna cast that stupid thought down. You might imagine that God ordained Christmas and Valentine’s Day; we are going to cast that imagination down. You might imagine a woman is set over the man; we are going to cast that dumb thought down. You might imagine it is okay for a woman to show her TNA when she walks down the street; we are going to cast that imagination down.

“And every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God”: anything that exalts itself above the Bible, our job is to cast it down. “And bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ”: we got to bring every man’s and every woman’s thought to obey God’s laws.

“And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.” That means we got to start with us first, the individual, the man in the mirror. Start with him and her first, then you can do the rest.

“At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to destroy it”: so we are telling America, Babylon the Great, according to Revelation 18, that America shall be burned with fire. That is the prophecy. It is not my personal feeling; my emotion has nothing to do with it. When the prophets saw it they wept, their belly trembled, they didn’t want to be alive, that is how terrible and dreadful it was. It has nothing to do with our personal feelings. Our job is to prophesy.

“If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.” That is referring to the nation of Israel, us, returning to the Lord God.

“And at what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to build and to plant it; If it do evil in my sight, that it obey not my voice, then I will repent of the good, wherewith I said I would benefit them.” That referred to us: he tore us down for breaking his laws, and that judgment now goes on all the other nations.

“For I will set mine eyes upon them for good”: he is setting his eyes upon the Israelites for good, that’s us. “And I will bring them again to this land”: so America is not our final destination. “And I will build them, and not pull them down”: God said he will build us and not pull us down. “And I will plant them, and not pluck them up.”

“And I will give them an heart to know me”: he is going to change our mind. That is what is going on now; he is changing the way we think, the way we act, the way we talk. “That I am the Lord: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God: for they shall return unto me with their whole heart.” That is the prophecy we are in the midst of right now.

“I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem”: brothers, you are the watchmen. Not only are you ambassadors; the Bible calls all of us watchmen. The watchmen are the ones that stand on the castle top and look for the enemy, to see if danger is approaching.

“Which shall never hold their peace day nor night”: as watchmen we are never to hold our peace. That means we got to pray three times a day, and we got to teach from sun up to sun down. This is why we teach three times a day, seven days a week. People ask why we teach so much: we are fulfilling prophecy. “Ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence”.

“And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” We are to give the Lord no rest. That means we got to pray and teach, and pray and teach, and pray and teach.

“Having your conversation honest among the Gentiles”: the Gentile means all people in a Gentile state of mind. But what we always tend to forget is the word honest. Some of us in here are natural born liars.

“Whereas they speak against you as evildoers”: our people in a Gentile state of mind, who are following a white man, speak evil against us. That’s a hate group, they ain’t right, they murder people, they rape people, they don’t have jobs. Wait a minute: they are teaching family, order in the family, the husband and wife together, the husband the head of the house, raising them children properly. The man don’t work, he don’t eat. Education, learn your history. They are cleaning up the communities, literally putting up missing persons posters everywhere, doing youth violence seminars. What do you mean a hate group? Oh, you mad because they are telling you the truth about history, what America did to the ancestors. That’s why they are a hate group.

“They may by your good works, which they shall behold”: you are always being watched, whether at your job, at your home or on the street. Somebody knows you are an Israelite, brothers and sisters. Somebody is watching you.

“Glorify God in the day of visitation.” Why would they glorify God in the day of visitation? Because they watched your example. ‘This brother, this sister, I watched them for months, almost a doggone year. I never told them I was watching them, but I listened to that honest conversation and I watched the way they conducted themselves. Maybe there’s something to that Bible. Let me check it out. I think the Lord brought that brother and that sister into my life.’

Listen good, remember, as ambassadors: “Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers”. Brothers and sisters, they are going to speak evil of us as evildoers. Remember they called Christ Beelzebub, the lord of the flies. Christ said if they call me names, how much more are they going to call you: you murderers, you liars, you thieves, you’re all homosexuals.

“They may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.” They will be ashamed. That’s why I worry about these other Israelite camps: they will be ashamed in that day, every last one of them, because they don’t know the Bible; they read right through this. ‘Oh, all of you are homosexuals, you murder people.’ Shut up.

That is why we all got to have a good conscience. I got a good conscience. I know we ain’t murdering nobody, and I ain’t worried about that. The hell is this?

“But chiefly them that walk after the flesh”: walking after the flesh we read in Galatians 5: fornication, hatred, witchcraft, uncleanness, emulations, variance, lasciviousness, drunkenness, things of that nature. “In the lust of uncleanness, and despise government”: the government Peter is talking about is God’s government, Christ’s government. They despise that thing and speak evil against it.

“Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.” Another word for dignities is ambassadors. They ain’t worried about speaking against the Bishops, the deacons, the captains, the officers: ‘the hell with you, we gonna stand outside the school and curse you out.’ That is what this is talking about. They speak against Christ’s government, and they are not afraid to speak evil of the dignities of Christ, the ambassadors.

It’s hard for black people, dignity. ‘Girl, I drink your bath water’: you have no dignity. The hell is this?

Dignity is formal reserve or seriousness of manner, appearance or language; the quality or state of being worthy, honored or esteemed; a high rank, office or position; a legal title of nobility or honor. In that time the dignities were the apostles, the disciples and Christ. Now we got the Bishops, deacons, captains, officers and soldiers, and people speak evil of them. That is what the scriptures say.

“For there shall be a day, that the watchmen upon the mount Ephraim shall cry”: so Ephraim are watchmen as well. They shall cry, “Arise ye, and let us go up to Zion unto the Lord our God.” The watchmen are going to be saying repent, let’s wake up and return to Zion.

“Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations”: one of the chiefest of nations now is America. “Publish ye, praise ye, and say, O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel.” It doesn’t say save all nations on the planet earth. He said go among the nations and say, save the remnant of Israel.

“Behold, I will bring them from the north country”: from North America. “And gather them from the coasts of the earth”: the coasts of the earth are places like Puerto Rico and Santo Domingo. “And with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither.” The prophecy is that a great company of Ephraim shall return.

“They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Israel”, and Ephraim is his heir.
“Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations”, “and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.”

“For the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, and ransomed him from the hand of him that was stronger than he.” He is going to ransom us from the white man. The white man is the one that is stronger than us, with his military. The Lord is going to destroy Babylon and deliver us from all the nations that have us captive, because all these nations are stronger than us.

We are the government that has no power: no military, no economic power, no political power. We have no power at all except this Bible, and brother, that’s all we need.

“In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen”: the tabernacle of David is being raised up now. “And close up the breaches thereof”: God is closing up the breaches. “And I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”: he is going to rebuild Israel as in the days of old. That means the twelve tribes ruling the earth.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom”: we are going to possess that white man. “And of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.” The ones called by God’s name are the Jews and the Christians. Those called by his name are all going into captivity, every last one of them.

precepts.why:
The same thing in the New Testament: “And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”.

It says the same exact thing as Amos. That is what the apostles were all about: rebuilding the tabernacle of David that was fallen down.

From the rebuilding of the tabernacle of David that was fallen down: “And I will cause the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel to return, and will build them, as at the first.” Do you see that? He will build us again as at the first. That’s the prophecy, the same as building it ‘as in the days of old.’

“And I will restore thy judges as at the first”: the first is talking about the time of Moses. “And thy counsellors as at the beginning”. When the Lord raises up the tabernacle of David, he restores Israel’s judges and counsellors as they were from the time of Moses.

As ambassadors, our job is to remind our people where we have fallen from and where we are going, and to let the nations know judgment is coming for them based on what they did to our people.

“And out of them shall proceed thanksgiving and the voice of them that make merry”: out of us shall proceed thanksgiving. “And I will multiply them, and they shall not be few”: we gonna fill this earth, brothers and sisters. “I will also glorify them, and they shall not be small”: we won’t be small, in number or in stature.

“Their children also shall be as aforetime, and their congregation shall be established before me, and I will punish all that oppress them.” Highlight that part: he will punish all that oppress us.

“And their nobles shall be of themselves”: our nobles shall be of our own people. We’re not going to have nobles or diplomats of other races, other nations. “And their governor shall proceed from the midst of them”: our governor, and that’s Christ. “And ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.”

“Behold, the whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury, a continuing whirlwind: it shall fall with pain upon the head of the wicked.” There’s going to be constant judgment upon the wicked. “The fierce anger of the Lord shall not return, until he have done it, and until he have performed the intents of his heart: in the latter days ye shall consider it.” So don’t be looking for no pie in the sky, no sunshine for the nations. In the latter days ye shall consider it; that’s why when we prophesy, things happen, things pop off amongst the nations.

sense.text:
“I beheld till the thrones were cast down”: Daniel beheld the kingdoms of the world thrown down. He saw America thrown down, Britain thrown down, China thrown down, Saudi Arabia thrown down, India thrown down, Pakistan thrown down, Germany thrown down. Every nation thrown down; that’s what Daniel said.

“And the Ancient of days did sit”: that’s the Lord. “Whose garment was white as snow”: he has a garment on, and if he got a garment, he has a body. “And the hair of his head like the pure wool.” So what is God, brothers? A black man.

“His throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.” So you can’t just walk up to the Lord and say, ‘hey Lord, let me have a conversation with you.’ That don’t happen. There’s order, there’s rank, there’s structure. In front of the Lord is fire all around him.

“A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.” The judgment is set, and the books are open.
“I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake”: that horn is America. The class stopped right there; America was not the subject for that day.

The king had a dream about an image, and Daniel is explaining to him what the dream means. “But as for me, this secret is not revealed to me for any wisdom that I have more than any living”: that’s Daniel speaking.

“Thou, O king, sawest, and behold a great image.” The king saw a great image, “whose brightness was excellent”, and “the form thereof was terrible.” “This image’s head was of fine gold, his breast and his arms of silver, his belly and his thighs of brass, His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay.”
“This is the dream; and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the king.” Now Daniel is going to break it down for him.

“Thou, O king, art a king of kings: for the God of heaven hath given thee a kingdom, power, and strength, and glory.” “Thou art this head of gold.” So Nebuchadnezzar represents Babylon the great, the head of gold, 605 to 539 BC.

“And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee”: the kingdom that came up next was Persia and Media, 539 to 331 BC. “And another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth”: that was the Greeks under Alexander the Greek, 331 to 168 BC.

“And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron: forasmuch as iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things”: that next kingdom was Rome, 168 BC to 193 AD. Some scholars say 476, but in 476 it was our people ruling at that time. That’s why we say 193 AD: that’s when Septimius Severus overthrew the Roman Empire, and they sat on the throne.

“And whereas thou sawest the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron”: write this down. The feet are America and Britain; America is a foot, Britain is another foot. Then you got the EU, NATO: that’s the ten toes.

“The kingdom shall be divided; but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron.” “And as the toes of the feet were part of iron”: because the military here in America is strong. “And part of clay”: Daniel explains the clay in the next verse. “So the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.”

What does the miry clay represent? “They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men”: all nations are here. The seed of men is here, in America and in Britain.

“But they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay.” There will be no true solidarity. This is why you see races and nations pop up, ‘what about this, what about that.’ There will be no true cohesion here in America or in Britain. It’s not going to happen.

“And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed.” In the days of these kings: in the days of America, in the days of NATO. It’s come, and America ain’t destroyed yet. This is what you’re seeing now, like we read in Psalms 50, ‘I will set them in order before your eyes’, because Israel is in this kingdom. We are an unseen government being established right before their eyes.

“Which shall never be destroyed”: this is why we are so bold to say, white man, you can’t stop this. It don’t matter who he kill amongst us, he can’t stop this truth, this teaching. If just one of you are left alive, the Lord gonna start it up, he gonna bring the word out again. This is like that mustard seed Christ spoke about.

“And the kingdom shall not be left to other people.” You know what that mean? Your white friend ain’t gonna rule with us. Your Arab friend ain’t ruling with us. Your East Indian friend ain’t ruling with us. That explains what about the white man and what about the other nations: this is not going to be their kingdom. It’s not for them.

What are we gonna do to the other nations? “But it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms.” America shall be broken and consumed. Britain shall be broken and consumed. The European Union shall be broken and consumed. NATO shall be broken and consumed. None of those nations are ruling with us in the coming kingdom. It’s our kingdom, “and it shall stand for ever.”

“Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands”: who’s this stone, brothers? This stone is Christ.

“And that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.” The feet and the toes represent all that was discussed in this class, and the feet also go into what we went through with the sub-Saharan slave trade and the transatlantic: it’s all in the feet. That’s the latter end of this kingdom, and Christ the stone is going to destroy all these kingdoms.

precepts.why: The stone that smote the image is Christ. “Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.” The stone the builders disallowed is the stone cut out without hands that breaks the kingdoms in pieces.
Christ is that rock: “they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” That rock is who, brothers? Christ, the stone of Daniel 2.

“And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.” He’s the chief corner what, brothers? The chief corner stone: the stone cut out of the mountain without hands is Christ.

sense.text:
Put this in your artillery. “And it shall come to pass, that as ye were a curse among the heathen”: that’s where we were, cursed among the heathen. “O house of Judah, and house of Israel; so will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing.” So he’s not saving all nations. We gotta kill that thought now: he’s not saving all nations.

“Fear not, but let your hands be strong.” Why did the Lord say fear not? Because we’re going to have opposition. He said fear not, but only let your hands be strong.

“But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar off, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be in rest.” Jacob shall return, and we gonna be in rest, “and at ease”: we gonna be at ease. “And none shall make him afraid”: nobody’s gonna make us afraid ever, ever again.

“For I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee.” Brothers and sisters, y’all so worried about the other nations. God said, I’m gonna make a full end of them. He’s not saving them; he’s gonna make an end of them.

“But I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure; yet will I not leave thee wholly unpunished.” Notice the difference between us and the nations. He will make a full end of all the nations whither he has driven us, but he will not make a full end of us. Israelites, we always gonna be around.

The first thought you might have is, oh, that just means he’s going to take away their power. It’s always deeper than that. When he says he’s going to make a full end of them, he means exactly what he says.

precepts.why:
Get mad, go call your mama now. Too damn bad. The Lord already said he’s gonna make a full end of those nations, and here’s the precept: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain.” That’s why the Lord said your thoughts ain’t my thoughts. You want to forgive everybody and forget; that ain’t what the Bible says. He said let the multitude perish that was born in vain. They are nothing, brothers and sisters. That’s what God says.

“And let my grape be kept, and my plant”: we’re the grape, the elect. “For with great labour have I made it perfect”: God has made us perfect with great labour. He makes a full end of the multitude, but his grape he keeps.

sense.text:
Going to the last book of the Bible for another precept to the full end of the nations: “And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” Then the question is, who’s written in the book?

Read it again, and a lot of them are scared. Only a few understand it; the rest are confused. ‘What are you talking about? I got friends that have jobs, my job does good to me, master’s been good to me. What do you mean they’re gonna be done away with?’ They’re gonna be done away with, brothers and sisters, every last one of them. They’re going into slavery, y’all deal with that, but go past slavery: what happens at the very end? They’re all done away with, every last one of them.

precepts.why: Who’s written in the book? “And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.” Who’s Daniel’s people, brothers? The Israelites. It says every one that shall be found written in the book: Daniel’s people are the ones written in the book.

Another precept, in case you’re doubting. Some of you are Christians: ‘I’m a Christian, I don’t know if I accept that. The hell would you? This is ludicrous, I’ve never heard this before.’ Listen up: “And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem.” Written among the living where? In Jerusalem. Only the Israelites are written, brothers. So whosoever was not found written in the book of life, cast into the lake of fire, is the nations.

sense.text:
Listen good, because the kingdom shall be established: the unseen government, the nation of Israel, the true nation of Israel shall be established, and here’s the prophecy. “But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established in the top of the mountains.” Didn’t we just read in the book of Daniel chapter 2 that in the days of those kings the God of heaven shall set up a kingdom, and it shall break in pieces all those kingdoms? We’re in that time. Don’t fear, brothers, just be strong.

“And it shall be exalted above the hills”: that means above the smaller governments. “And people shall flow unto it”: the people is the Israelites, flowing unto it.

“And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord”: these are the remnant of the Israelites coming up to the mountain of the Lord, “and to the house of the God of Jacob”, because we’re going to have the top economy on the planet.

“For the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.” See what’s going to be taught: the law shall go forth of Zion.

“And he shall judge among many people”: see, now come the other nations. “And rebuke strong nations afar off”: this is what we read about, that stone will break them in pieces.

“Nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.” Everybody talking about they want peace on earth. There will be no peace on earth until the twelve tribes of Israel are established again in this earth. That’s what the Bible said.
“But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid”: none gonna make us afraid. “For the mouth of the Lord of hosts hath spoken it.”

“For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the Lord our God for ever and ever.” You know what that implies? Christ said ‘well done’ in Luke 19: ‘be thou lord over ten cities’, be thou lord over five, be thou lord over two. Everyone is going to follow you. You will be their god; they will worship you, and you will give them orders, and you will return to the Lord, the King of kings and Lord of lords, because you will be the ambassador on a whole nother level. Some don’t get it: ‘the hell is this, me a god? No, it’s impossible.’

precepts.why:
What does it mean, all people will walk every one in the name of his god? “I have said, Ye are gods”: God said we are gods. “And all of you are children of the most High”: all of us are children of the Most High.

“But ye shall die like men”: we have died like men; we’re in slavery right now. “And fall like one of the princes”: we have fallen like one of the princes.

sense.text: What about the other nations? “And had a wall great and high”: the kingdom, the capital of the earth, shall have a wall great and high. “And had twelve gates”: there’s going to be twelve gates. “And at the gates twelve angels”: twelve angels at these gates. “And names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”: the names on the kingdom, brothers and sisters, are the twelve tribes of Israel.

“On the east three gates”: three gates, like Judah, Benjamin, Levi. “On the north three gates”: like Ephraim, Simeon, Zebulun. “On the south three gates”, like Issachar, “and on the west three gates”: another three tribes.

“And the wall of the city had twelve foundations”: there’s gonna be twelve foundations, “and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.” Those twelve apostles are going to be the top of the 144. Those twelve will be the leaders of the 144, meaning they’re in it, but they’re the top guys.

“And he that talked with me had a golden reed to measure the city, and the gates thereof, and the wall thereof.” “And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth”: the length of the city is the same distance as the height of the city. “And he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs”: write this down, twelve thousand furlongs is 1,500 miles. “The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” That’s why the pictures of the kingdom look like a square.

That is our carnal, fleshly imagination, what we came up with trying to figure out what it might look like. The Lord’s gonna do it in a whole other way, because he already said eye hasn’t seen and ear hasn’t heard what God has prepared for those that love him. The pictures show all the people coming up, Israel coming from everywhere, because we’re gonna have the top economy.
